title: release-publish accepts registry tokens in process arguments
reasoning: The executor exposes a `token` option and, despite warning that it leaks, still passes the secret as `cargo publish --token <value>`. Redacting the console log only protects nxrust's own output; the token remains visible in process command-line inspection, CI process snapshots, shell/task telemetry, and any wrapper that records argv. A release executor should not provide a footgun for publishing credentials when Cargo already supports `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN`.
reproduction: Configure or invoke `@eddacraft/nxrust:release-publish` with `{ "token": "secret" }`; while the process is running, inspect the cargo child command line and the token is present as the value following `--token`.
recommendation: Remove or reject the `token` option, or translate it into a child-process environment variable before spawning Cargo so the token is never placed on argv. Prefer documenting `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN` as the only supported credential path.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No included release-publish tests are listed, and the available cargo argument tests focus on general argument construction rather than secret handling for the publish executor.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a release-publish executor test that passes `token` and asserts the spawned cargo argv never contains the token value; either expect an error or expect the token to be supplied via environment only.
minimumFixScope: Update `src/executors/release-publish/executor.ts` and, if environment injection is chosen, the cargo process helper API used by `src/utils/cargo.ts`/`src/utils/run-process.ts`.
